questions.prompt: What does an availability zone protect against?

options.text: A single-datacenter (zone-level) failure within a region
A bug in your application code
A slow internet connection at the user's home

questions.explanation: Availability zones are physically separate locations within a region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking, so one zone failing doesn't take the others down.

questions.prompt: Which factors should guide your choice of region? Select all that apply.

options.text: Whether the services and sizes you need are available there

questions.explanation: All four matter: proximity/latency, service availability, price differences, and where data must legally reside.

questions.prompt: Two regions in the same geography that some services use for disaster recovery are called a region ____.
questions.explanation: A region pair is two regions in a geography used by some services to replicate for disaster recovery. Not every region has a pair.

questions.prompt: Order these from the SMALLEST unit to the LARGEST.
questions.explanation: Datacenters make up a region; a geography contains one or more regions and preserves data-residency boundaries.

questions.prompt: Match each infrastructure term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A set of nearby datacenters you deploy into
A physically separate, independently powered location in a region
An isolated Azure instance such as Azure Government

questions.explanation: Regions are groups of datacenters; zones are independent locations within a region; geographies preserve residency; sovereign clouds are isolated instances.
